AbstractText.Label: INTRODUCTION
AbstractText.content: Deficiency of Treg cells and hyperactivity of Th17 cells together are involved in the immunological pathogenesis of asthma. The adenosine A2AR plays a critical role in the increased Foxp3 expression of Treg cells and the decreased Th17 generation.

AbstractText.Label: OBJECTIVE
AbstractText.content: The study aimed to investigate A2AR expression in peripheral blood and its regulatory effect on balance of Treg/Th17 cells in asthma.

AbstractText.Label: METHODS
AbstractText.content: 31 patients with chronic persistent asthma were recruited and divided into 18 intermittent to mild asthma patients, 13 moderate to severe asthma patients. A2AR, Foxp3 and ROR-γt mRNA expression levels in PBMCs were measured by qPCR. TGF-ß, IL-17 and IgE in plasma were detected with ELISA. 42 BALB/c mice were randomly, equally assigned to control group, OVA group and OVA+CGS (CGS21680, A2AR agonist) group. The infiltration of lung inflammation cells were evaluated by HE, A2AR, Foxp3 and ROR-γt mRNA in lung tissues measured by qPCR, TGF-ß, IL-17 and IgE in plasma measured with ELISA, and IL-17 and TGF-β protein in lung tissues analyzed with IHC.

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: Our results showed that expression A2AR mRNA in PBMCs was associated with asthma severity. Foxp3 mRNA, TGF-ß and FEV1%pred positively correlated with A2AR mRNA in asthma. ROR-γt mRNA and IL-17 negatively correlated with A2AR mRNA in asthma. CGS could promote Foxp3 mRNA expression, TGF-ß and improve lung function while inhibit ROR-γt mRNA expression, IL-17 and the infiltration of lung inflammation cells.

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSION
AbstractText.content: A2AR could regulate the balance of Treg/Th17 cells in asthma. This article is protected by copyright. All rights reserved.
